extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/practitioners preparing or responding to appeals
extracted.subtask_short: patent appeal brief and examiner answer
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and evaluating appeal briefs, amendments, affidavits/evidence, and examiner's answers in USPTO patent application appeals (procedures under 37 CFR and MPEP). Covers required brief contents/format, admission of post-appeal amendments/evidence, appeal-conference and examiner-answer content and new-ground procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix copy presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal. The copy of the claims should be a clean copy and should not include any markings such as brackets or underlining except for claims in a reissue application and a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy of the claims should be double-spaced and the appendix should start on a new page. See MPEP §1454 (reissue claims presentation), 37 CFR 1.530(d) and (f) (reexamination), MPEP §2274 (ex parte reexamination) and MPEP §2675 (inter partes reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum brief contents and order (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) specifies the minimum requirements for a brief; a brief is in compliance as long as it includes items (i) to (v) in the order set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appellant may include in the brief a list of references, table of contents, table of cases, copies of evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon in the brief, etc., but the minimum items (i)-(v) must appear and be in the specified order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including non-admitted amendments/evidence in brief (37 CFR 41.37(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(2) prohibits the inclusion in a brief of any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appellant wishes to seek review of an examiner’s refusal to admit an amendment, affidavit or evidence, such review is by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181. The time for filing that petition is based on the date the examiner refused to enter the amendment/affidavit/evidence, not the date the brief is filed. Amendments filed with a brief must be submitted in a separate paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification page requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an Identification page setting forth the applicant’s name(s), the application number, the filing date of the application, the title of the invention, the name of the examiner, the art unit of the examiner and the title of the paper (i.e., Appeal Brief).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example format specifies that each required item (including the Identification page) should start on a separate page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents page(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Table of Contents page(s) as part of the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each required item (including the Table of Contents) should start on a separate page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest page(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Real party in interest page(s) identifying the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each required item should start on a separate page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals, interferences, and trials page(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include page(s) listing related appeals, interferences, and trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each required item should start on a separate page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter page(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Summary of claimed subject matter page(s) describing the claimed invention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each required item should start on a separate page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument page(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the Argument section on separate page(s) presenting appellant's substantive arguments directed to the claims and record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments must be directed to the claims and to the record as they appeared at the time of the appeal; headings/subheadings should be used (and examiner's response should mirror them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix page(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Claims appendix page(s) containing the clean, double-spaced copy of the appealed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claims appendix should start on a new page and comply with the clean-copy/no-markings rule (except as noted for reissue/reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief must be directed to claims and the record as of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be directed to the claims and to the record of the case as they appeared at the time of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appellant wishes to remove claims from consideration on appeal, the appellant must submit an amendment to cancel the claims (see 37 CFR 41.31(c) and 37 CFR 41.33). Choosing not to present arguments or rely upon particular evidence as to certain claim rejections results in waiver of those arguments/evidence for purposes of the appeal and the Board may summarily sustain any grounds of rejection not argued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board determination of compliance and correction process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board determines whether appeal briefs comply with 37 CFR 41.37 and completes the determination (generally) within approximately one month from filing of the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief is compliant or contains only minor informalities, the Board will accept it and forward it to the examiner. If non-compliant, the Board will send a notice requiring a corrected brief and appellant must file a corrected brief within the time set in the notice to avoid dismissal. If appellant disagrees with a noncompliance holding, a petition under 37 CFR 41.3 may be filed, but filing a petition does not toll the time for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after appeal but before brief (37 CFR 41.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after the date of filing an appeal and prior to the date a brief is filed may be admitted as provided in 37 CFR 1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new amendment must be submitted in a separate paper. Entry of a new amendment in an application on appeal is not a matter of right. Admitted amendments may be to cancel claims, comply with form requirements, present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal, or amend the specification or claims upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented (see 37 CFR 41.33(a)). If denied, examiner should use PTOL-303 to notify applicant of non-entry and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed on or after filing a brief (37 CFR 41.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief may be admitted only to: (1) cancel claims where cancellation does not affect scope of any other pending claim, or (2) rewrite dependent claims into independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(2) provides that a brief shall not include any non-admitted amendment. Amendments filed with a brief must be in a separate paper. Rewriting dependent claims into independent form includes (A) adding parent claim limitations to a dependent claim to make it independent, and (B) rewriting an independent claim to incorporate a dependent claim's subject matter and canceling the dependent claim; examiners use PTOL-304 to notify applicant of non-entry after filing a brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner response and entry of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must respond to all amendments filed after an appeal has been taken and prior to transfer of jurisdiction to the Board under 37 CFR 41.35(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner indicates in an advisory action that an amendment would be entered, the examiner must state how individual rejections set forth in the final Office action will be impacted (except where amendment merely cancels claims). If the examiner determines an amendment clearly places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the amendment and allow the application. Except for amendments meeting conditions noted, all other amendments submitted after the filing of a notice of appeal will not be entered except as permitted by specified regulations (e.g., 37 CFR 41.39(b)(1), 41.50...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of affidavits or other evidence after appeal but before brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or other evidence submitted after the date of filing a notice of appeal but prior to the date of filing a brief may be admitted if the examiner determines that the affidavit or other evidence overcomes all rejections under appeal and that a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the affidavit or other evidence is necessary and was not earlier presented has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner denies entry, use PTOL-303 to notify applicant. If the evidence places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter and allow. All other affidavits/evidence filed after the date of filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by specified regs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/evidence after filing brief and treatment of IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or other evidence filed after the date of filing a brief are generally not admitted except as permitted by regulations; Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) submitted after the date of a notice of appeal are normally held in abeyance pending decision on the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of IDS is based on MPEP §609 and 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, not on 37 CFR 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: No consideration by examiner of amendments/evidence after jurisdiction passes to Board
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment, affidavit or other evidence received after jurisdiction has passed to the Board should not be considered by the examiner unless remanded for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§1210 and 1211.02 for remand procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and form of examiner's answer (headings and order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer should include, under appropriate headings and in the indicated order, items such as: Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal, Response to Argument, Withdrawn Rejections, New Grounds of Rejection, and a Conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must state that every ground of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified by any advisory action and pre-appeal brief conference decision) is being maintained unless expressly withdrawn. The Response to Argument must state whether the examiner disagrees with each of appellant's arguments and explain reasons for any disagreement, using headings/subheadings paralleling appellant's brief. Examiner's answers should be furnished within two months after receipt of the brief. Examiners may use specified form paragraphs (e.g., 12.254.01, 12.254.02, 12.255, 12.256, 12.257, 12.279.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of withdrawn rejections and unargued rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the subheading 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS,' the examiner should list any grounds of rejection that are being withdrawn. The examiner must treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal and maintain all rejections set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken, unless appellant has overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant did not present any argument on a rejection in the appeal brief, the examiner should maintain the rejection in the examiner’s answer and identify that the appellant has not argued the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: New grounds of rejection in examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection, but any rejection that relies upon evidence not relied upon in the Office action shall be designated as a new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New grounds of rejection must be prominently identified and must be approved by the Director (delegated to TC Directors or designee). For each new ground, a complete explanation supporting the rejection must be provided with proper reference to the applicable statute, prior art references relied upon, and the claim numbers affected. If an answer contains a new ground, the applicant has TWO MONTHS to either reopen prosecution (request reopening under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment/evidence) or maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief addressing each new ground per 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv); reply briefs may not be accompanied by amendments/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference requirement and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases in which an acceptable brief has been filed (except when the examiner charged with preparing the answer reaches the conclusion that the appeal should not go forward and the SPE approves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should include the examiner preparing the answer, a supervisory patent examiner (SPE), and another examiner (conferee) experienced enough to assist. During the conference, consideration should be given to dropping cumulative art rejections and eliminating technical rejections of doubtful value. The examiner responsible for preparing the answer should include the names and initials of the conferees on the answer so the record is clear that a conference has been held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits/declarations/exhibits filed with notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or exhibits filed with the notice of appeal should be treated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an affidavit/declaration/exhibit was refused entry under 1.116 or prohibited by 41.33, the examiner should not comment on it in the examiner's answer. It would be improper for appellant to rely on material not entered. If appellant has grounds to challenge non-entry, file a timely petition under 37 CFR 1.181. Affidavits swearing behind a reference should be identified as considered under 37 CFR 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations for foreign-language documents relied upon by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document relied upon by the examiner is in a language other than English, a translation must be obtained so the record is clear as to the precise facts relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translation may be a machine translation or an English equivalent. See MPEP §706.02 for reliance upon abstracts and foreign language documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding examiner's answer that includes new interpretation of law
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of existing patent law, the examiner’s answer, application file, and an explanatory memorandum should be forwarded to the TC Director for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved by the TC Director, the examiner's answer should be forwarded to the Office of the Associate Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for final approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to pay appeal forwarding fee (37 CFR 41.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of an appeal forwarding fee is required within the time permitted by 37 CFR 41.45(a) to avoid dismissal of the appeal in any application or ex parte reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee requirement may be avoided if appellant had timely paid the fee for filing a brief required by 37 CFR 41.20(b) in effect on March 18, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' obligation to identify how final rejections apply to amended/added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 would be entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must identify (in an advisory action) how one or more individual rejections set forth in the final rejection would be used to reject the added or amended claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification is required to make clear how the final rejection would be applied to the newly added or amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on citing unpublished decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: No unpublished decisions which are unavailable to the general public by reason of 35 U.S.C. 122(a) can be cited by the examiner or the appellant, except that either may cite an unpublished decision in an application having common ownership with the application on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All correspondence with the Board must be on the record; unpublished decisions unavailable to the public generally cannot be relied upon in the appeal record.
